statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Alberta Corporate Registry via CORES (Corporate Online Services) and Search and Reservation System, administered by Service Alberta and Red Tape Reduction
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: All Alberta statutory registration forms must be completed in English or French; the entity name must use Latin script letters, and any non-Latin source name must be transliterated into English characters before reservation; the corporate designation 'Limited Partnership', 'LP', or 'L.P.' must appear as the correct legal suffix for the entity type.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon name rejection, the applicant receives a formal notice stating the statutory grounds for refusal under the Alberta Partnership Act and corporate registry policy; the applicant may file a written administrative appeal with Service Alberta and Red Tape Reduction within 30 days of the rejection notice, providing a fresh NUANS report and documentary evidence rebutting the objection; if the administrative appeal is unsuccessful, the applicant may apply for judicial review before the Court of King's Bench of Alberta within 6 months of the final decision or within the applicable limitation period.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Virtual office services are permissible only when the provider maintains a physical street address physically located in Alberta and accepts service of process and mail forwarding on behalf of the Limited Partnership; a P.O. Box alone is not acceptable; for an e-commerce FPV racing drone retail business operating through PayPal and Stripe, a mail-forwarding virtual office is generally acceptable, but financial institutions and payment processors may require supplementary evidence of operational presence and a physical address for merchant underwriting and chargeback management.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low probability of unannounced physical inspection, quantified at approximately 3-5% annual likelihood for a non-public-facing e-commerce entity; the Alberta Corporate Registry does not routinely conduct random physical inspections absent a complaint, tax flag, or apparent compliance breach; a remote office for online retail further reduces the operational inspection risk to minimal levels.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry – Service Alberta (online Name Search)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a name search request through the Alberta Corporate Registry portal for the proposed limited partnership name. Provide owner identification and formal name request; if using an extra-provincial name, attach a notarized certificate of name. Retain the reserved name confirmation letter for filing.
required_dossiers: Government-issued photo ID of general partner
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected due to conflict or misleading element, file a new name request with two alternate names within 10 business days; no formal appeal is available until the final rejection is issued.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Limited Partnership Agreement and Capital Subscriptions
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Legal counsel / Notary public (private drafting; no government filing required)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft and execute a limited partnership agreement specifying general and limited partner rights, capital contribution schedule, profit and loss allocation, management authority, and dissolution events. The agreement should be notarized for evidentiary completeness and retained for registry review on demand.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Correct any missing consents or contribution schedules by executing amended schedules; no adverse regulatory action occurs at this private drafting stage.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry – Service Alberta (online registration / paper filing counter)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete and submit the Registration of Limited Partnership form at the Alberta Corporate Registry. Attach the name reservation approval, the executed partnership agreement, and the consents of the registered office and registered agent. Pay the state filing fee and receive the registration certificate.
required_dossiers: Consent to serve as registered office / registered agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registrar raises a deficiency or requests clarification, submit the required amended form or supporting explanation via the portal within 15 business days; late cure may require repayment of the fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax Registrations and Business Number Activation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA); Alberta Tax and Revenue Administration
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Using the LP registration certificate, apply online or by Form RC1 for a CRA Business Number (BN) and register for GST/HST, payroll, and corporate income tax accounts as applicable. Register with Alberta Tax and Revenue Administration for Alberta corporate tax and, if employing staff, for workers' compensation (WCB).
required_dossiers: General partner's contact and identification details
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If CRA defers or rejects the BN application, verify the legal entity name and general partner identifiers; resubmit corrected Form RC1 or request manual registration through CRA's Business Registration line.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Municipal Business Licence and Occupancy Clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local municipal licensing authority (e.g., City of Calgary or City of Edmonton business licence office)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After securing the leased premises, file a municipal business licence application for the manufacturing and retail operation. Provide zoning clearance, proof of building occupancy, and, if triggered, a fire safety inspection. Obtain a certificate of occupancy before conducting carbon-fiber milling or drone assembly.
required_dossiers: Lease agreement or proof of premises
Zoning approval / letter of no objection
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the municipality imposes additional conditions (e.g., ventilation or sprinkler retrofit), complete the required upgrade and submit a compliance verification letter to lift the licence hold.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA / Agence du revenu du Canada, ARC) administers federal income tax and GST/HST registration, return filing, audits, and refunds; online service portal: CRA 'My Business Account' (Mon dossier d'entreprise). Alberta has no provincial VAT/PST and does not operate a separate provincial sales tax registration; Alberta corporate income tax applicable to corporate partners is assessed and collected by CRA under a federal-provincial tax collection agreement. The statutory creation or extra-provincial registration of the Alberta limited partnership is effected through the Alberta Corporate Registry (Service Alberta) under the Partnerships Act (Alberta).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: 1) Determine whether the Alberta LP carries on business in Canada or otherwise makes taxable supplies in Canada; any person engaged in commercial activity, including an Alberta LP (a 'person' for Excise Tax Act purposes), that exceeds the small-supplier threshold of CAD 30,000 in worldwide taxable supplies in the preceding four consecutive calendar quarters is required to register for GST/HST. 2) Register or extra-provincially register the LP at the Alberta Corporate Registry (Service Alberta); obtain the Alberta registration particulars (foreign partners are permitted and no minimum capital contribution is statutory). 3) Apply to CRA for a 9-digit Business Number (BN) and program accounts through 'Register a business' or My Business Account; typical accounts are GST/HST (RT), import/export (RM), and payroll (RP) where employees exist; non-resident entities and foreign partners without a Canadian establishment use Form RC1 (Request for a Business Number), the CRA non-resident registration procedure, and, where required, appoint a Canadian representative with relevant powers. 4) Upon issuance of the RT program account, the LP must issue GST-registered invoices in its own name, file periodic GST/HST returns (GST34) electronically via GST NETFILE or GST EDI, and maintain its BN on customs and export documents. 5) Voluntary registration is available below the small-supplier threshold and is generally advisable for an exporter of FPV drones so that input tax credits can be claimed and outbound supplies can be zero-rated.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Pass_Through_Eligible — For Income Tax Act purposes the Alberta LP is not a taxpayer; income, gains, losses, and credits flow through to partners pro rata under ITA s. 96, and Alberta does not impose entity-level income or capital taxation on the partnership. Alberta's 8% provincial corporate income tax applies, where relevant, only to corporate partners with a permanent establishment in Alberta. Non-resident partners carrying on business in Canada through the LP are taxable on their share of Canadian-source partnership income, and non-resident corporate partners are subject to Part I tax under s. 115 read with the partnership rules. For GST/HST, however, the LP itself is treated as a registrable person and must charge GST on taxable supplies made in Canada; this dual classification (flow-through for income tax, separate person for GST/HST) is fundamental to the Canadian hybrid classification framework.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No 'check-the-box' or elective entity-classification regime exists under Canadian federal tax law; classification is statutory and follows the legal form of the entity. Principal statutory elections relevant to an Alberta LP are: (i) ITA s. 97(2) election to transfer property to the partnership on a tax-deferred rollover basis; (ii) ITA s. 249.1(4) election permitting the partnership to adopt a non-calendar fiscal period; (iii) GST/HST reporting-period options aligning the LP's remittance frequency with its fiscal year (monthly, quarterly, or annual); and (iv) elections for a capacity to file GST/HST returns on a consolidated/group basis where the LP and its corporate partners satisfy ETA grouping conditions. Hybrid-mismatch rules in ITA ss. 18.4-18.6 apply automatically based on the deduction/non-inclusion outcomes of the partners' jurisdictions and are not elective; publicly traded limited partnerships that meet the SIFT definition are taxed at entity level under the SIFT rules and cannot affirmatively elect out of SIFT status.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: GST/HST (Goods and Services Tax / Harmonized Sales Tax) under the Excise Tax Act; only the 5% federal GST applies in Alberta because Alberta has no provincial sales tax and is not a participating HST province.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000 — the small-supplier threshold based on total worldwide taxable supplies (including zero-rated supplies) in the immediately preceding four consecutive calendar quarters; once exceeded, mandatory GST/HST registration applies to the Alberta LP. Voluntary registration is permitted below the threshold and is typically elected by export-oriented businesses to claim input tax credits and zero-rate exports.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time fiscal clearance, mandatory government API, or digital stamping regime exists in Canada. CRA requires GST/HST returns to be filed electronically for most registrants (mandatory for registrants with annual gross revenue exceeding CAD 1 million, via GST NETFILE, GST34 electronic filings, or approved GST EDI software). E-invoicing is voluntary and is being harmonized through the Pan-Canadian E-invoicing standard (PEPPOL BIS 3.0). Taxpayers must retain complete source documents and electronic audit trails for at least six years in CRA-acceptable format, and CRA may request system-level access during a GST/HST or export audit.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Supplies of FPV racing drone goods qualify for zero-rating under s. 1(a) of Part V, Schedule VI to the Excise Tax Act when the goods are exported by the supplier as part of the supply. The supplier must be a GST/HST registrant, the goods must be delivered to a common carrier for export (or otherwise exported) before the recipient takes possession or use in Canada, and the goods must leave Canada within a reasonable time (CRA administrative practice accepts a 60-day export window for most commercial shipments). The supplier must retain contemporaneous proof of export, including commercial shipping documents and, where required by the Canada Border Services Agency (CBSA), a B13A export declaration or automated export reporting. Related services supplied to non-residents, such as software/telemetry licensing, engineering drawings, or warranty services performed entirely outside Canada, may also be zero-rated under the offshore-services provisions of Part V, Schedule VI. Domestic sales within Canada remain taxable at 5% GST.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: CBSA export declaration (Form B13A Canada Customs Export Declaration) or automated export reporting where the shipment meets CBSA reporting thresholds
Bill of lading / air waybill showing the consignee address outside Canada and evidencing departure of the goods from Canada
Commercial invoice with the FPV drone item description, unit pricing, Incoterms, and an explicit 'GST/HST zero-rated export supply' notation referencing the LP's GST/HST registration number
Signed sales contract or purchase order from the non-resident buyer governing price, delivery, and payment terms

Payment evidence such as SWIFT MT103, bank foreign-exchange transaction record or inward remittance record, or PayPal/Stripe settlement reports demonstrating receipt of export proceeds from the foreign buyer
Courier waybill, exporter's internal shipping log, or customs broker summary for low-value courier shipments where a B13A is not mandatory
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: CRA may reassess GST/HST within four years (unlimited where misrepresentation, neglect, or fraud is established), deny zero-rating, disallow refunds, and re-characterize an export supply as taxable at 5% where proof-of-export documentation is missing, inconsistent, or backdated. The resulting assessment carries unremitted GST plus prescribed daily compound interest. Penalties include failure-to-file and failure-to-remit sanctions and the false-statement penalty under ETA s. 280(2) of up to 25% of the tax that would have been assessed had the facts been as stated. For income tax, a gross-negligence or fraud penalty of up to 50% of understated Part I tax may be imposed on partners under ITA s. 163(2). Exporters with repeat deficiencies may be placed on a CRA export audit profile, have refunds offset, and be subject to criminal prosecution for willful evasion. All export records must be retained for six years under ETA s. 286. As a factual clarification, Canada does not currently impose a statutory 180-day export-proceeds repatriation deadline for goods; the 180-day figure is a conservative treasury and documentary benchmark that should be contractually supported by payment terms and reflected in the LP's accounts receivable aging records.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada) is the central monetary and financial system authority. Canada does not maintain a dedicated foreign exchange administration or exchange-control authority. The Department of Finance Canada supervises currency policy, OSFI regulates federally chartered deposit-taking institutions, and FINTRAC enforces the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act for anti-money laundering and cross-border funds reporting.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Canada is an IMF Article VIII member and maintains full current and capital account convertibility. The Canadian dollar is freely floating and there are no exchange-control approvals required for dividends, management fees, loan repayments, equity redemptions, or capital repatriation. A non-resident limited partner of an Alberta limited partnership may nevertheless be subject to Canadian Part XIII withholding tax on distributions characterized as interest, rents, royalties, or certain payments, and non-resident partners carrying on business in Canada through the LP may be required to file Canadian income tax returns. Profit remittance is not blocked, but the transaction must satisfy the applicable income tax treaty position, transfer pricing rules, thin capitalization rules, and bank anti-money laundering due diligence. There is no requirement to purchase Canadian dollars through a central counterparty or to secure regulatory approval for FX conversion.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Canada imposes no statutory export proceeds surrender requirement and no mandatory conversion ratio. Exporters may lawfully retain foreign currency proceeds in Canadian bank accounts, foreign currency accounts, or offshore accounts. For Canadian income tax purposes, export revenue included in the LP's income must be converted into Canadian dollars using a reasonable exchange rate methodology, generally the rate prevailing on the relevant inclusion date. Cross-border financial transfers equal to or exceeding C$10,000 or the foreign-currency equivalent are reportable to FINTRAC by financial institutions and money service businesses as electronic funds transfer reports, while currency transactions of C$10,000 or more trigger currency transaction reports. Export documentation should remain aligned with Canada Border Services Agency requirements, Global Affairs Canada trade controls, and the LP's customs export declarations.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium viability for operational payment rails; low viability as the primary regulated account or capital escrow account. Foreign digital EMI providers, including cross-border neobanks and payment platforms, are not chartered banks under the Canadian Bank Act and cannot provide Bank of Canada clearing membership or Canadian deposit insurance. They may operate if registered as money service businesses with FINTRAC, comply with the Retail Payment Activities Act, and partner with a Schedule I or II Canadian bank for local settlement. Such platforms can provide valuable multi-currency collection, vendor payout, and low-value trade disbursement services, but treasury policy should maintain a Canadian-bank primary relationship for capital contributions, liquidity concentration, tax remittances, and payroll.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Remote account opening is generally permitted by Canadian banks, provided the applicant meets enhanced due diligence standards. There is no absolute statutory requirement that every partner or director appear physically; however, most Alberta banking institutions require at least one authorized signatory, the general partner, or a designated officer to complete identity verification through a notarized or bank-branch interview for complex or non-resident structures. In practice, a corporate general partner's directors must provide valid government-issued identification and proof of address, the Alberta LP must produce a current Alberta Corporate Registry extract and its limited partnership agreement, and foreign partners with 25% or greater ownership must be identified as beneficial owners. Non-resident documentation generally requires notarization, apostille under the Hague Convention, and recent translations certified by an accredited translator. Some banks will permit full video-based KYC with liveness verification and digital signatures, but a physical interview may be imposed where beneficial ownership is layered or where the counterparty jurisdiction carries elevated ML/TF risk.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident limited partner or beneficial owner holding 25% or greater interest without a Canadian credit footprint or verifiable local presence.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified passport, residential address proof dated within 90 days, government-issued photo identification, bank reference letter, six months of bank statements, source-of-wealth and source-of-funds letters, tax identification number, curriculum vitae or business profile for material owners, and notarized or apostilled copies of all foreign identity and address documents.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Tiered or opaque ownership structure involving trusts, nominees, or intermediate holding entities that obscures the ultimate beneficial owner.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Full organizational chart through every ownership layer, registered partner register, partnership agreement extracts, trust deed or nominee declaration, register of individuals with significant control or equivalent, confirmation that no bearer shares exist, and a legal opinion from licensed Canadian counsel confirming the natural persons with direct or indirect control of the LP.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: FPV drone product line perceived as dual-use, export-controlled, or subject to aviation safety licensing requirements.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Representations and warranties that the business sells hobby racing drones and components, product datasheets, FCC and ISED certification evidence, Transport Canada exemption or compliance summary if applicable, Global Affairs Canada export control classification, CBSA tariff classification codes, end-user attestations, and a compliance memorandum confirming that no products are classified as controlled goods or destined for sanctioned parties.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Initial capital injection from a jurisdiction with AML/CFT deficiencies or routed through a high-risk intermediary bank.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Direct wire confirmation from the remitting bank, correspondingly thorough source-of-funds narrative, intermediary bank chain disclosures, sanctions screening reports, FATF jurisdiction assessment, and a complete transaction trail evidencing the economic substance of the capital contribution.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Online retail revenue received through PayPal and Stripe without integrated bank reconciliations or with elevated chargeback risk.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Payment processor settlement statements, monthly payout summaries, chargeback ratio below processor thresholds, website terms of sale, refund and return policies, invoice-level sales ledger, customer dispute log, and up-to-date PCI-DSS compliance attestation for the e-commerce stack.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Non-resident limited partner capital contributions should be routed via SWIFT MT103 from a FATF-compliant correspondent bank directly to the LP's primary Schedule I bank account in Canada. Remittance instructions should identify the LP legal name, account number, and the purpose as limited partnership capital contribution for the ISIC 3240 FPV racing drone business. The receiving bank will screen all parties against sanctions lists and will report any incoming EFT or electronic funds transfer of C$10,000 or more to FINTRAC. The LP should be prepared to provide the executed limited partnership agreement, capital contribution schedule, beneficial ownership forms, source-of-funds documentation, partnership tax registration data, and a copy of the partnership return if already filed. The payer must avoid crypto-based transfers, third-party payment processors, or multi-hop intermediary structures, as such routing will almost always trigger extended hold periods or refusal. Contributions in foreign currency may be converted to CAD at the bank's prevailing spot FX rate, and any conversion should be documented for capital account recording.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For direct supplier and vendor payment in support of carbon-fiber milling and brushless motor integration, the LP should use SWIFT MT103 for straightforward cross-border wire disbursements, including inventory purchases, tooling, and logistics. For larger or documentary transactions, the LP should use commercial letters of credit, typically initiated through MT700 and amended via MT707, with supporting invoices, packing lists, bills of lading, certificates of origin, insurance certificates, and inspection reports. Domestic operating payments and payroll should settle through Payments Canada rails, including ACSS, LVTS, or the Real-Time Rail where available. Low-value cross-border payouts may be executed through regulated money service businesses such as Wise, Airwallex, or Currencycloud, provided such entities are FINTRAC-registered and the bank account remains the master operating account. Retail revenue from PayPal and Stripe should be settled into the LP's operating account in CAD or USD on a scheduled payout cycle and reconciled against the bank ledger. Any outbound transfer of C$10,000 or more must be captured by the bank's FINTRAC reporting, and all counterparties must undergo sanctions screening and beneficial ownership verification.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Spot USD/CAD and other major currency conversions for immediate settlement of commercial invoices and capital transactions
Outright US Dollar / Canadian Dollar forward foreign exchange contracts, typically executed under a bank master FX agreement or ISDA, for trade receivables and inventory purchasing up to 24 months
Flexible or window forwards that allow early or late delivery within a specified period for estimated cross-border cash flows

Cash-settled non-deliverable forwards, restricted to circumstances where the underlying currency is not freely deliverable or where a Canadian Schedule I dealer confirms commercial necessity; standard CAD/USD NDFs are not required because the Canadian dollar is fully convertible
Cross-currency swaps and FX swaps for intercompany financing, capital structure hedging, and matching of foreign-currency assets and liabilities
Vanilla FX options, collars, participating forwards, and zero-cost structures with regulated Canadian deposit-taking institutions or licensed investment dealers

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry (Service Alberta, Director under the Partnership Act)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days after each anniversary date of the limited partnership's registration.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing fee of CAD 150 (approx. USD 110); non-filing for two consecutive annual cycles triggers administrative strike-off after the Registrar issues not less than 30 days' notice; reinstatement requires all arrears and outstanding returns to be filed.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Canada Revenue Agency T5013 Partnership Information Return (T5013 Summary and T5013 slips) - required if the LP meets the CRA partnership filing thresholds
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For a fiscal period ending on December 31, on or before March 31 of the following calendar year; for any other fiscal period end, on or before the last day of the fifth month after the fiscal period end.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file a required T5013 return attracts a penalty of CAD 25 per day, minimum CAD 100, maximum CAD 2,500, under Income Tax Act section 162(7)(c); continued non-compliance may lead to a CRA compliance order and, in serious cases, summary prosecution and additional gross-negligence penalties.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No automatic statutory audit requirement for a private Alberta limited partnership under the Partnership Act. A mandatory independent audit is triggered only when the LP is a reporting issuer under Canadian securities law, when the partnership agreement or a majority of limited partners requires audited financial statements, or when a partner or regulator specifically requests an audit under the partnership agreement or applicable securities legislation.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Canadian private enterprises prepare financial statements in accordance with CPA Canada Handbook - Accounting Standard for Private Enterprises (ASPE); IFRS applies if the LP is a reporting issuer or the partnership agreement elects IFRS. Record keeping must also meet CRA books-and-records requirements under Income Tax Act section 230.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Alberta does not require a public beneficial-ownership filing for limited partnerships. The LP must maintain an internal register of all general and limited partners, with contributions, profit-sharing ratios, and transfer dates. Every transfer of a partnership interest must be recorded on an ongoing basis; any change in general or limited partner identity or contribution is reflected in an amended declaration filed with the Alberta Registrar. The LP annual return confirms general partner identity, registered office, and principal place of business, without publicly disclosing limited partners.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of General and Limited Partners
Register of Partnership Interests and Transfers
Minute Book of Partnership Resolutions and Unanimous Consents

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 23% combined federal (15%) + Alberta (8%) general corporate income tax rate in Alberta; the Limited Partnership is fiscally transparent under section 96 ITA, so the headline rate applies at the partner level (corporate or individual), not to the LP itself.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Federal Manufacturing and Processing profits tax reduction (federal rate 13% effective for qualifying M&P activities); Federal Small Business Deduction (9% federal rate on first CAD 500,000 of active business income for Canadian-controlled private corporation (CCPC) partners); Alberta Small Business Deduction (2% Alberta rate on first CAD 500,000 taxable income for qualifying CCPC partners); full deductibility of R&D expenditures and generous Scientific Research and Experimental Development (SR&ED) investment tax credits up to 15% (non-refundable) or up to 35% (refundable for CCPCs under taxable capital limits); Atlantic Investment Tax Credit does not apply in Alberta. All incentives are computed and claimed at the partner level on the partner's tax return due to the pass-through nature of the LP.
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_limit_years: 20 years forward / 3 years carryback for non-capital losses; capital losses carry forward indefinitely (deductible only against taxable capital gains); at-risk limitation rules for limited partners under subsection 96(2.1)-(2.4) restrict deductible losses to the partner's at-risk amount.
corporate_income_tax_regime.note: The schema template erroneously suggested 5 years; the legally correct Canadian limit is 20 years for non-capital losses (subsection 111(1)(a) ITA).
